Carrying debt increased by USD 5130 million, while reported EBITDA rose from USD 3148 million to USD 3813 million. Prior gross leverage was 6.27x versus current 6.53x; prior net leverage was 5.17x versus reported current 4.88x and October distribution-adjusted 6.02x. Debt financing and cash timing therefore move leverage in different directions.
Better earnings do not establish persistent deleveraging when new debt and distributions absorb the benefit. The apparent net improvement reverses after the known payment.
Net cash interest cover improved from 2.71x to 3.29x because EBITDA expanded while net cash interest paid was broadly stable. Accrued net interest expense nevertheless exceeds cash paid.
Current service capacity has strengthened, but payment timing and net interest income prevent the current cash yield from being treated as an all-in prospective borrowing cost.

FY2024 levered FCF is USD 1880 million, but FY2024 dividends and equivalents are USD 2038 million and acquisitions use USD 2347 million. Discretionary cash flow after distributions is USD -158 million before acquisitions.
Cash conversion is meaningful, but allocation is not self-funding after shareholder payments and acquisitions; external financing rather than operating weakness explains the growing debt burden.

The issuer states USD 2919 million of cash liquidity after the October distribution, versus USD 7267 million before it. Its long-term debt ladder shows USD 93 million due in FY2025 but excludes the USD 487 million short-term receivables facility and finance leases.
The known payment leaves meaningful resources, not the headline year-end buffer; near-term funding analysis must include the receivables renewal and cannot rely on the long-term ladder alone.

Customer contract liabilities are USD 177 million, compared with USD 87 million previously. Acquisitions and advance receipts contribute; the obligation is future performance rather than ordinary supplier credit.

Advance funding temporarily supports cash but requires delivery without equivalent fresh cash collections; organic float growth and future unwind are not established. It is not financial debt or a covenant basket.

Goodwill and other intangible assets total USD 13865 million, against negative equity. Reported EBITDA, operating EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined are distinct, and the adjusted earnings measure is not audited as a GAAP performance subtotal.
Book assets and adjusted earnings are not interchangeable with liquidation support or debt-service cash. Neither recovery value nor legal headroom is established by these accounts.

The strongest contrary evidence is the combination of expanding earnings, improving cash-interest coverage, substantial post-distribution liquidity and a long interval before the next term-loan or note maturity. This would support a more benign creditor interpretation if subsequent cash generation were retained and the receivables facility renewed without constraining collections. The observed preference for acquisitions and special distributions prevents treating that outcome as established.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–57; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 150–153; calculation C32

A time-aware downside begins if customer collections slow or inventory requirements rise after the distribution. Receivables and inventory would consume operating cash first; eligible-receivables constraints could simultaneously reduce funding flexibility as the short-term facility approaches renewal. With less cash retained, net leverage would rise even before an earnings decline, and refinancing dependence would move forward from the longer-dated loan and note maturities. Observable triggers are renewed receivables and inventory cash absorption, lower facility availability, further shareholder distributions and failure to renew the receivables funding line. No numerical stress is imposed.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 123; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 150–153

This is a retrospective annual financial foundation, not an independent credit recommendation, valuation or covenant-capacity opinion. Source readiness confirms the issuer, fiscal scope and publication boundary; the accepted inventory does not establish market prices, legal permissions or unrestricted access to every cash balance. No separate industrial-versus-finance division is identified in the inspected consolidated presentation; receivables financing is included as issuer debt, not treated as a matched-funded finance subsidiary.

The full statement panel is limited to the selected annual baseline. Older annual comparative amounts are retained only where needed for directional calculations; the supplied within-year filings and later quarterly operating results are not merged into it. Consequently, seasonal cash-generation patterns, discrete-quarter changes and a complete multiyear statement history are not established here. Later events are limited to those expressly identified in the annual report, rather than a complete subsequent-period cash roll.

- High severity: the annual report was published after the assessment date and the information cutoff is unspecified. The figures support a retrospective fiscal snapshot, not proof of what investors knew at that date. A defined cutoff and contemporaneously available filings would close that distinction.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- High severity: dated comparable security prices, peer observations and controlling legal documents are absent. Neither executable relative value nor operative covenant capacity, collateral sharing or recovery can be inferred from these financial ratios. Matched market observations and operative agreements are required for those conclusions.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- High severity: the full repayment perimeter is incomplete. The maturity ladder excludes receivables financing and finance leases; exact maturity days and amortisation are not established for several notes, the revolving facility, government advances and the newest term-loan tranche. Relative rank for receivables financing, government advances and finance leases is also unestablished, so they are excluded from the rank chart, not from total debt. Instrument carrying values are unavailable by individual loan tranche, and the revolving commitment-to-availability difference is not assumed to be cash drawn. Complete payment, guarantee and security schedules would close these gaps.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 144–153; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 171–172

- High severity: reported cash is not certified as entirely unrestricted or freely transferable, and the combined October payment and receivables draw have no fully specified sequence or complete subsequent cash roll. The common dividend payment day is known, but the equivalent-payment and draw days are not established. Cash-access evidence and a dated treasury roll would be needed to convert the bounded event adjustments into a complete near-term liquidity bridge.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 120–120; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 33; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 152; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 170

- Medium severity: only the selected annual statement panel is reproduced. Earlier annual figures serve limited comparisons, while the within-year filings have not been independently extracted into a complete quarterly or cumulative history. Seasonality, quarter-to-year summation and constructed interim earnings are therefore not established. A period-aligned historical panel would close this coverage limitation without changing directly reported annual figures.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 121–123

- Medium severity: no separate FFO definition, gross cash coupon amount, gross interest expense, interest income or unlevered cash-flow tax shield is established. FFO coverage, FFO to debt and unlevered FCF remain unavailable rather than being estimated from a differently defined operating subtotal. Supplemental interest and tax reconciliations and an explicit FFO definition would close those distinctions.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 71–71; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 121–123

- Medium severity: maintenance and growth capex, separately isolated disposal cash proceeds, the aggregate pension obligation, restricted cash and short-term investments are not established by the extracted statement lines. Complete seniority subtotals are also not source-printed or certified here. These gaps limit maintenance cash-flow, asset-access and total fixed-obligation analysis; detailed schedules would close them. No absent amount is treated as zero.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 120–123; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 145–156

- Medium severity: adjusted earnings contain issuer-grouped add-backs whose recurrence, cash realisation and detailed components are not fully established. The customer-funding increase is also partly acquisition-related, so its organic contribution and unwind timing are not established. Detailed adjustment and customer-advance schedules would be needed before treating either as sustainable debt-service support.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 71; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 142

- Low severity: source dashes for discontinued operations, related per-share data, retirement-plan settlement items, share repurchases and revolving repayments remain missing quantities. The reported totals and numeric-component checks agree, but this does not establish those individual observations as explicit zeros. Clarified issuer schedules would close those presentation gaps.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 121–123

- Low severity: the issuer’s aggregate asset-and-liability adjustment in its EBITDA reconciliation is not mapped precisely to the individually disclosed cash-flow movements. The distinct definitions are retained; the explicitly defined operating working-capital subset, not an inferred reconciliation plug, anchors run-rate inputs. A component-level reconciliation would close the difference.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 71; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 123; calculation C16; calculation C29

- Low severity: corporate revenue is not separately quantified, and a comparable operating-KPI history has not been extracted. Segment external-sales totals reconcile without an invented corporate zero. Additional segment and operating schedules would be required for a broader operational trend assessment.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 164–165
